summary: Complete target-level continuation of RS.0: native root pullback and its section-compatible tensor-power comparison; an equivalence between actual chosen-frame root objects and the accepted framed coordinate groupoid; full labelled-arrow realization of affine charts, fppf local normalization and stackification comparison; frame descent, arbitrary finite coefficient-chain coherence and explicit universe adapters. The accepted parent algebra and generic upstream sheaf infrastructure are reused, not replanned. The plan is complete with named supplier requests and a typed-signature boundary; it makes no implementation claim.

nodes.title: Section-compatible pullback of root tensor powers
nodes.statement: For h:Y→T, an invertible sheaf M on T and n≥0, construct κ(h,M,n):(h*M)^n≅h*(M^n), natural in actual line isomorphisms. Use the inverse of the unit comparison at n=0 and the tensor comparison recursively at n+1, with M^0=O and M^(n+1)=M^n⊗M. It carries (h*t)^n to h*(t^n). Under any chosen frames its section equation is the image under the coefficient ring map of z^n; it is compatible with identity and composite pullback through the supplier’s strong monoidal comparisons.
hypotheses: T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.
Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.

The exponent may be zero. Global-section pullback is the map obtained from the unit of module pullback–pushforward, or equivalently from the image of a morphism O→M, not an assumed isomorphism on global sections.

Fix the imported comparison directions as β₀:h*O_T≅O_Y and β₂:h*(M⊗N)≅h*M⊗h*N. Thus κ₀=β₀⁻¹ and each successor uses β₂⁻¹; these are inverses of the strong monoidal structural maps where that convention is used.
proofSteps: Import the strong monoidal module pullback and tensorSection from AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A, restricted to native rank one by L0B/SF.3. This is the existing generic operation, not a new monoidal structure.
At zero use O_Y≅h*O_T; in the successor step use κ_n⊗id followed by the inverse of the strong monoidal tensor comparison. The parent fixes parentheses and transport of line isomorphisms.

Apply the imported sectionwise tensor/pullback equation at each successor and the unit-section equation at zero. This induction supplies the root-specific section law; it does not require global sections to commute with tensor products as an isomorphism.
Identity/composition compatibility follows from the supplier’s monoidal unit and tensor diagrams, not from declaring different tensor powers equal.
acceptance: The n=0 section is one under the actual unit comparison.
The comparison retains its direction (h*M)^n→h*(M^n).

sources.match: Root identifications require transporting actual tensor powers across a test-scheme morphism. The displayed section equation is our recursive deduction, not a separately numbered theorem in Appendix B.

sources.locator: L0A–L0B; Suggested.lean tensorSection, tensorUnitIso, pullbackModulesMonoidal and pullbackFiniteLocallyFreeObjIso (unpaginated)

nodes.title: Pullback of native root objects and arrows
nodes.statement: For n≥1 and (L,s) on T, define h*:Root(T,L,s,n)→Root(Y,h*L,h*s,n). Send (M,t,φ) to (h*M,h*t,h*φ∘κ(h,M,n)); send a root arrow a to h*a. The two arrow conditions are preservation of the section and φ_target∘a^n=φ_source. The resulting functor preserves both conditions and all automorphism labels. Given an isomorphism of target pairs, transport the last identification by that isomorphism; do not change the root section.
hypotheses: T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.
Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.
n≥1; Root is the parent’s root-object groupoid, with only invertible line maps as arrows.
proofSteps: Use the parent root-object definition without redefining its carrier. Apply native line pullback to M and every isomorphism, and the supplier’s section pullback to t and s.
Compose κ with the pulled φ. The power-pullback section equation and functoriality give φ′(t′^n)=s′.
Apply pullback to each arrow square and use κ’s naturality; the separate pulled section equation proves the other arrow condition. Identity and composition are the inherited functor laws.
An isomorphism of target pairs gives a root functor by composing φ with the target line isomorphism; the assertion on s verifies its object equation.
acceptance: No flatness condition is imposed on h.
A nonidentity automorphism can become identity under pullback.

sources.match: The root moduli problems pull back along test morphisms; these explicit formulas spell out the native functor and the two equations which the source leaves implicit.

nodes.title: Coherent root pullback on the scheme site
nodes.statement: For a fixed scheme X and (L,s) on X, T→X maps to Root(T,L_T,s_T,n) with L_T=T*L and s_T=T*s. The root pullback functors form a groupoid-valued pseudofunctor on (Sch/X)^op. Its identity and composition natural isomorphisms have the native line-pullback identity and composition isomorphisms as underlying components, corrected on the target L_T by the same comparisons. They preserve sections and root identifications. The triangle and pentagon hold, and every finite iterated pullback agrees with direct pullback through these specified comparisons.
hypotheses: T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.
Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.
Fix n≥1. Coherence is equality of the specified natural transformations after associators; no strict equality of chosen pullback objects is asserted.
proofSteps: Restrict the supplier’s coherent native Picard pullback to roots using the section law and κ-composition law. Correct both the root line and the pulled target line; correcting only M gives an ill-typed φ square.
For identities use the native unit comparison. For a pair of morphisms use the native composition comparison on M and L and its compatibility with the n-th power.

Underlying line isomorphisms satisfy triangle and pentagon by the supplier’s coherence. Equality of root arrows reduces to their underlying line maps, because the two preservation conditions are properties.
Induct on a finite chain; the pentagon compares all bracketings. This is the general root-object coherence target beyond the parent’s chosen affine two- and three-step comparisons.
acceptance: The n=1 root functor has the identity-pair groupoid behaviour.
A four-map chain has equal composite comparison arrows for all parenthesizations.
Nonflat coefficient change preserves these diagrams even when it identifies distinct arrows.

sources.match: The object description is base-change compatible. Our proof uses the imported monoidal pseudofunctor coherence to make this compatibility precise.

sources.locator: §3, Remark 3.1 and Proposition 3.4, pp. 12–13; Corollary 3.13, p. 16
sources.match: Proposition 3.4 gives finite root base-change compatibility in the logarithmic setting; it motivates, rather than supplies in native Lean, the pair-level comparison here.

nodes.title: Native root objects with chosen line frames
nodes.statement: Fix a commutative ring B, n≥1 and a target pair (L,s) on Spec B with specified frame l:L≅O. Let f∈B be the coordinate of s through l and Scheme.ΓSpecIso. A FramedNativeRoot object is a parent root object (M,t,φ) together with e:M≅O. A morphism between (a,e_a) and (b,e_b) is any root arrow a→b: it need not preserve e_a,e_b. Composition and inverses are those of the parent root groupoid. Forgetting e is fully faithful; its essential image consists exactly of roots whose line M is globally trivializable.
hypotheses: B may be the zero ring, or nonreduced; f is arbitrary.
The target frame l is fixed. Frames are data on objects, not an additional preservation condition on arrows.
proofSteps: Add e as object data and use the parent Hom type unchanged, so the groupoid laws are inherited.
The forgetful Hom map is the identity on actual root arrows and hence fully faithful. Essential-image membership is exactly existence of e; no affine Picard group is presumed zero.
For two frames on the same root, the identity root arrow is an isomorphism of the two framed objects. A frame-preserving arrow restriction would destroy this comparison.
acceptance: Both e_a,e_b appear when computing the scalar label of an arrow.
The category is not the groupoid of roots with frame-preserving arrows.

sources.match: Appendix B.2 supplies the native triples. Adding a chosen line frame and retaining all root arrows is our coordinate-comparison construction, not a source definition of a globally trivial root stack.

The comparison can read every native root arrow as a unit label.

nodes.title: Equivalence of native framed roots and coordinate roots
nodes.statement: With B,f,n,l as in FramedNativeRoot, construct a groupoid equivalence E_l:FramedNativeRoot(B,L,s,n,l)≌FramedRoot(f,n,B) from the parent. For (M,t,φ,e), set y=coord(e(t)), and let u be the unit coefficient of l∘φ∘(e^{-1})^n∘c_n^{-1}:O≅O. Then u*y^n=f. For an arrow h:a→b, its label w is the unit scalar of e_b∘h∘e_a^{-1}. The label satisfies y_b=w*y_a and u_b*w^n=u_a. Conversely any such w gives exactly the root arrow e_b^{-1}∘mul(w)∘e_a. The inverse on objects uses M=O, t with coordinate y, e=id, and φ=l^{-1}∘mul(u)∘c_n. Unit and counit are actual root isomorphisms with the underlying frames; both triangles hold.
hypotheses: n≥1, B arbitrary commutative, l a specified target line frame.
Coordinates include the canonical free-PUnit-to-unit and ΓSpec comparisons; Γ(Spec B,O) is not identified definitionally with B.
proofSteps: Reuse current native line coordinates and unit-scalar automorphism equivalence; at the old pins the coordinate bridge is the parent’s freeHomEquiv/freePUnitIsoUnit route. Generic tensorSection and section/unit comparisons are imported through JAC-A-RS0.

The parent section-power-in-trivialization law turns the root equation into u*y^n=f. Its proof is induction: zero has coordinate1 and successor uses the imported pure-tensor coordinate multiplication, then c_(n+1).

The parent root-arrow scalar law gives both arrow equations. In the reverse direction, the section equation verifies h(t_a)=t_b and the coefficient equation verifies φ_b∘h^n=φ_a on the basis of O^n. Checking only a section does not verify the power-identification square.
Every automorphism of the trivial module is multiplication by a unique unit, so the two Hom maps are inverse and preserve labels, identities, composition and inverses.
Construct the inverse objects as stated. The frame e gives the native root isomorphism to the reconstructed object; the unit/counit triangles reduce to actual line-frame inverse identities.
acceptance: Full faithfulness is a bijection of labelled arrows, including at y=0.
No n-th root of u is chosen in this equivalence.
For u=3,y=1,n=2,f=3 over Z/4 the equivalence has an object, although the normalized chart has no B-point.
For n=2,f=0 over Z/9 the roots y=3 and y=0 remain nonisomorphic.

sources.match: The triple definition and local quotient calculation support this coordinate deduction. The unit coefficient and complete Hom equivalence make the implicit trivialization computation explicit. The corrected exponent d from inherited E12 is used.

Realizes the accepted coordinate chart as actual native root data.

nodes.title: Coordinates under changes of source and target frames
nodes.statement: If e′=mul(a)∘e and l′=mul(b)∘l for units a,b∈Bˣ, the same root has coordinates y′=a*y, u′=b*u*a^{-n}, f′=b*f. This induces a groupoid equivalence from the framed coordinates for l to those for l′, with object formula (u,y)↦(b*u,y) when e is retained. Changing root frames e_p,e_q by a_p,a_q changes an arrow label to w′=a_q*w*a_p^{-1}. Both arrow equations are preserved. Root-frame changes with b=1 are connected by the identity native root arrow, whose coordinate label between the two readings is a. These comparisons have inverse unit formulas and composition cocycles.
hypotheses: Use the conventions of native-framed-equivalence. n≥1; no condition on section y.
The target unit b is common to the source and target of a root arrow.
proofSteps: Conjugate the scalar power identification by c_n and the two changed frames. The parent section-power transport gives (mul(a))^n=mul(a^n) under c_n, so the coefficient becomes b*u*a^{-n}.
Conjugating e_q∘h∘e_p^{-1} gives w′=a_q*w*a_p^{-1}. Substitute this into both arrow equations; cancel only the named units.
Compose frame changes by multiplying a and b. The identity native root arrow compares different readings of the same root, and its power square supplies u′*a^n=b*u.
These are calculations from the imported section/unit comparison, not new general scalar-automorphism or tensor coherence APIs.
acceptance: At y=0 the u equation still carries information.
Over Q, n=2, u=1,y=1,f=1, a=2,b=1 gives u′=1/4,y′=2; omitting a^{-n} breaks the root equation.
For e_p changed by2 and e_q unchanged, w=1 becomes w′=1/2.
Target-frame changes require no root of b until one insists on normalized coefficient1.

sources.match: The G_m quotient and power action in B.1–B.2 lead to these gauge formulas. The signs and factors are authored computations with the fixed source/target coordinate conventions.

nodes.title: Native coordinates commute with arbitrary test-algebra change
nodes.statement: Fix A,f,n≥1 and the trivial target pair on Spec A. For every A-algebra map ψ:B→C, pull chosen native root frames along Spec ψ using the canonical pulled-unit comparison. The square between E_B,E_C, native framed-root pullback and the parent framedRootChange(ψ) commutes by a specified natural isomorphism. Coordinates become (ψ(u),ψ(y)); every arrow label becomes ψ(w). The natural isomorphism preserves both section and power identification, has the native pullback comparison as underlying line map, and obeys identity/composition coherence in ψ. It is compatible with the parent normalizationBaseChangeNatIso and normalization chart triangles.
hypotheses: A,B,C are arbitrary commutative rings, with the stated algebra maps; ψ need not be injective or flat.
The chosen target frame on every test is pulled from Spec A, so the coordinate of the target section is the image of f.
proofSteps: The supplier’s pulled-unit comparison transports e to a frame of the pulled line. The section map and ΓSpecIso_naturality identify its coordinate with ψ(y).
Transport the actual power-identification automorphism using κ; the unit and tensor coherence identify its image-of-one coefficient with ψ(u). The same argument for e_q∘h∘e_p^{-1} gives ψ(w).
Use the parent framed change functor rather than redefining ring substitution. Construct the square’s comparison as the actual pulled-line comparison and verify the two root-arrow equations.

Root pseudofunctor coherence proves identity/composition compatibility. The normalization algebra sends coefficients through ψ and T to T by the parent’s construction; its generator equations identify the normalization and chart triangles.
acceptance: Z/4→Z/2 kills y=2 and the nonidentity label−1 while all comparison diagrams commute.
The zero-ring spectrum gives empty-site computations without a Nontrivial ring assumption.
Wild characteristic is permitted; no assertion that μ_n is etale is used.

sources.match: Base change of the triple is described in Appendix B; coordinate naturality is deduced using the imported section and unit comparisons.

sources.locator: §3, Remark 3.1 and Proposition 3.4, pp. 12–13; Corollary 3.13, p. 16
sources.match: Proposition 3.4 confirms the expected finite-root base-change behaviour; our pair-level square explicitly includes all arrows.

nodes.title: The affine chart as actual native root data
nodes.statement: For A,f,n≥1 and every A-algebra B, construct C_B from the parent root-point action groupoid Q(B) to Root(Spec B,O,f,n). A point z with z^n=f becomes M=O, the section with coordinate z, and φ=c_n. An arrow labelled ζ∈μ_n(B) acts by multiplication by ζ on O. Its section and power squares give the actual root arrow. This is the composite of the parent normalized chart embedding, E_B^{-1} and forgetting the frame. It is fully faithful, but it need not be essentially surjective on B. These functors are pseudonatural on arbitrary test-algebra maps with the native comparisons of the preceding targets.
hypotheses: Q(B) is FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:RS.2/root-point-groupoid, retaining labelled arrows; use its actual root-point carrier.
The point z lies in the parent affine ring A[Z]/(Z^n−f) functor of points. No effective Cartier divisor hypothesis is used.
proofSteps: Apply the existing normalized chart embedding into FramedRoot; its coefficient is1 and its root coordinate is z.
Use the inverse native coordinate equivalence and forget the chosen frame. This gives the exact trivial line, section and c_n identification, with all scalar arrows intact.
Full faithfulness is the composite of the parent’s fully faithful embedding, the equivalence, and the fully faithful forgetful functor. Naturality uses native-coefficient-naturality.
The Z/4 obstruction and nontrivial root lines show why objectwise essential surjectivity is not asserted; the local normalization theorem supplies the relevant local statement.
acceptance: The full Hom bijection retains every stabilizer label.
The construction agrees with the native O and with the parent normalized FramedRoot inclusion.

nodes.title: Every native root has local normalized affine coordinates
nodes.statement: For any scheme T and native root (M,t,φ) of (L,s), n≥1, there is an fppf covering of T refining an affine Zariski covering which trivializes both M and L. On each affine member Spec B, native coordinates give (u,y) with u∈Bˣ and u*y^n=f. Refine it by the parent singleton cover Spec D→Spec B, D=B[T]/(T^n−u). The existing unit r=T in D has r^n=u, and the pulled root is isomorphic to the native chart image with coordinate r*y and coefficient1. The root isomorphism has label r. The construction retains both arrow equations and is stable under arbitrary pullback of test schemes; it asserts existence of local frames, not a functorially chosen global frame.
hypotheses: T is an arbitrary scheme; no reducedness, noetherianity or flatness of test changes is assumed.
Invertible sheaves, sections, tensor products and isomorphisms use the native Tau Ceti/Mathlib carriers.
n≥1. The family of affine trivializing opens can have arbitrary size allowed by the site; T need not be quasi-compact.
A positive exponent is essential for the finite-free unit-root cover; zero is not a covering exponent.
proofSteps: Use the existing local trivialization atlases of M and L, intersect their opens, and refine by affine opens. Restriction/pullback comparison with native modules comes from AlgebraicVectorBundles, not a new general local-freeness theory.
Read the two frames through the native equivalence. Apply the parent positive-exponent finite-free, finite-presentation and singleton-cover package to the unit coefficient u.

The parent normalized framed isomorphism has label r; its equations are r*y for the section and 1*r^n=u for the identification. Transport it back to a native root isomorphism using the Hom equivalence.

Zariski covers are fppf and the fppf precoverage is closed under composition and base change. Pull chosen covers back and use the parent Cartesian normalization square; no canonical global choice or flatness of the test change is needed.
acceptance: Z/4,n=2,u=3,y=1 normalizes over D although it cannot normalize over B.
If n=p in characteristic p, D still gives a valid fppf cover; no etale assertion is made.
At y=0 no cancellation by y occurs, so all μ_n stabilizers survive.
For a nonzero square-zero y its normalization r*y remains nonzero under the faithfully flat cover because r is a unit.

sources.match: The quotient presentation relies on local trivializations; this target supplies the exact root-specific cover and isomorphism.

sources.locator: Lemma 59.28.3, Tag 040N, complete proof; online, no fixed pagination

nodes.title: Affine action charts stackify to native root objects
nodes.statement: Fix A,f and n≥1. On the fppf site of affine A-schemes let Q be the parent μ_n action-groupoid prestack of points of Spec A[Z]/(Z^n−f), and R the restriction of the native root-object pseudofunctor for (O,f). The native chart realization Q→R is fully faithful on every fibre and locally essentially surjective. Using the parent root-fpqc-descent theorem and the imported stackification, its extension a_fppf(Q)→R is an equivalence of stacks in groupoids. Its unit/counit and base-change comparisons lift the actual labelled chart arrows and are pseudonatural in arbitrary coefficient maps. Restriction from the scheme site to the affine basis gives the same stack through the supplier’s site-basis comparison. This is the native comparison underlying the parent RS.1 affine-chart statement, not a new generic quotient or algebraicity theorem.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including nonreduced rings; n≥1 and f arbitrary.
Use the fppf topology and actual groupoid-valued pseudofunctors; the objectwise orbit set is not the input.
The native root stack is supplied by the parent descent target. Algebraic atlases, coarse spaces and DM criteria remain owned by RS.1 and its suppliers.
proofSteps: Reuse the parent fpqc root-descent theorem; its restriction is an fppf stack. Its exact module-descent supplier is R09.3, so effective descent is not inferred merely from a chart.
Full faithfulness follows from native-chart-realization and the Hom equations. Local essential surjectivity is native-local-normalization on the affine basis.

Apply Stacks Lemma8.9.1 via D0’s stackification: Q has sheaf Hom sets since it embeds fully faithfully into the stack R. The morphism Q→R has the two characterizing properties, so the induced stackification comparison is an equivalence.

The universal property gives the actual equivalence and invertible modifications; it also compares the coefficient-change extensions. Use the requested affine-basis comparison to extend to test schemes, rather than equating an affine site with the full site.
acceptance: The Z/4,f=3,n=2 root is a global object of the associated stack even though Q(B) is empty.
The zero-section automorphism sheaf is μ_n and persists after stackification.
Nonzero nilpotent root sections are not replaced by zero-section data.
The wild characteristic p dual-number unit1+ε survives as an arrow when ε^2=0 and n=p.

sources.match: The root-with-section affine quotient is the motivating statement; our comparison proves that it uses native triples and their arrows.

sources.locator: Lemmas 8.9.1–8.9.3, §8.9 Tag 02ZO and Lemma 8.9.1 Tag 02ZP; online, no fixed pagination
sources.match: Stackification retains sheafified Hom sets and adds locally represented objects; its universal property gives the comparison. No isomorphism-class sheaf replaces it.

nodes.title: Descent comparison for different target-line frames
nodes.statement: For an affine open with two target frames l and l′=mul(b)∘l, n≥1, the associated stacks of normalized charts with equations z^n=f and z′^n=b*f are canonically equivalent through their respective native-root comparisons. Explicitly, over B[R]/(R^n−b), the comparison is z′=R*z, and its inverse is z=R^{-1}*z′. On two choices R_1,R_2 the ratio R_2/R_1 lies in μ_n and supplies the chart-arrow modification. On triple frame overlaps those modifications satisfy the root-arrow cocycle, so the associated stack glues to the native root-object stack for a nontrivial target line. No global n-th root of b, equality of the two raw affine charts or globally selected compatible frame roots is required.
hypotheses: The frames concern the same target line with section; transitions are actual units. n≥1.
Charts are compared after fppf stackification; all comparison arrows and their cocycles are retained.
proofSteps: Use native-frame-change to identify framed coordinates under l,l′. The two stackification equivalences land in the same native root groupoid, so their composite defines the canonical stack equivalence.
Normalize the changed coefficient b with the positive-exponent Kummer cover. The direct native identity-arrow comparison reads as multiplication by R on normalized chart coordinates.
Ratios of two unit roots have n-th power1. They are the invertible modification between local chart maps; at zero sections their labels must still be recorded.

On triple overlaps compose the identity native root arrows; full faithfulness recovers their coordinate cocycle, even when chosen roots do not multiply strictly. Descend the equivalence, not an arbitrary chosen global root of the transition unit.
acceptance: Over Q,n=2,b=−1 the normalized raw chart equations f=1 and f′=−1 have different Q-points but their associated stacks describe the same native pair through the two target frames.
At z=0 two roots R_1,R_2 induce different μ_n modification labels although both section maps give0.
A four-open refinement gives the same descended comparison after the specified modifications.

sources.match: B.1–B.2 express the root moduli problem independently of trivializations. The transition-cover and ratio formulas are authored coordinate deductions.

sources.locator: Lemmas 8.9.1–8.9.3, §8.9 Tag 02ZO and Lemma 8.9.1 Tag 02ZP; online, no fixed pagination
sources.match: The universal comparison makes the frame-independent equivalence an equivalence of stacks, retaining the local modifications.

nodes.title: Coherence of normalization covers for arbitrary finite chains
nodes.statement: For a fixed parent framed root p and a finite chain of arbitrary test-algebra maps B_0→…→B_m, m≥0, use the parent normalization change maps to compare the normalization of the fully changed p with every parenthesization of the iterated chosen scheme pullback of its original cover. The comparison is the unique isomorphism with the prescribed projections to Spec B_m and the original normalization scheme. It agrees with the direct parent normalizationBaseChangeIso for the composite chain after each canonical pullback collapse. All forward/inverse projection formulas, naturality for every labelled framed arrow, insertion of identities and composition of chains agree; for n≥1 the normalized-chart triangle agrees as well. The scheme comparison alone allows n=0. This extends the accepted two- and three-step specifications rather than restating them.
hypotheses: No flatness or injectivity is imposed on any B_i→B_(i+1).
Use the native chosen pullbacks and their actual associator/pasting isomorphisms; no definitional equality of different chosen limits is asserted.
For n=0 no fppf-cover or chart-normalization claim is made.
proofSteps: Compose the parent normalization-change algebra maps. Identity and composition are already specified there, so coefficients and the adjoined root identify the direct composite map.
Inductively paste the Cartesian coefficient squares and use the native pullback universal property to form the comparison to each chosen bracketing.

Every comparison has the same two composite projections. Repeated pullback.hom_ext proves equality of comparison morphisms, inverses and all rebracketing diagrams; it also proves naturality in framed arrows using the parent natural isomorphism.
For n≥1 the parent chart triangle and the same projection characterization carry the normalized chart map through the finite composite. The proof never cancels the root section.
acceptance: m=0 gives the identity comparison, after the empty-chain convention.
m=2 and m=3 reproduce the parent comparisons on both projections and both inverse projections.
For a chain Z/4→Z/2→Z/2→Z/2→Z/2 all formulas hold although nilpotent sections and the −1 stabilizer collapse at its first map.
The n=0 algebra comparison remains valid without being a cover.

sources.locator: §3, Remark 3.1 and Proposition 3.4, pp. 12–13; Corollary 3.13, p. 16
sources.match: Proposition 3.4 motivates coefficient compatibility. The arbitrary finite chosen-limit coherence is our induction from the parent’s ring-map universality and native pullback uniqueness, not a printed root-stack theorem.

nodes.title: Root comparisons under coherent enlargement of ambient universes
nodes.statement: For a small scheme site and an enlargement u≤v, import the coherent universe-lift functor on schemes, native modules and invertible sheaves, together with section, tensor, Spec/Γ and pullback comparisons. Restrict the enlarged test site to the essential image of the original site. Applying these comparisons to the parent root data gives an equivalence between the original root groupoid and the lifted root groupoid, commuting with all arrows, frames, κ, chart realization and stackification. On a ring B this is the comparison with ULift B via the actual ring equivalence; units and root coordinates map through that equivalence. Identity and successive enlargement comparisons satisfy triangle/pentagon coherence. This statement is not an equivalence between all small and all larger test schemes.
hypotheses: Specify u≤v and the essential-image site, or an explicit small skeleton and its induced topology.
The supplier’s lift preserves the native geometric carriers and covering families and comes with coherent operation comparisons; a scalar-point wrapper alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Request generic native scheme/module universe comparisons from SF.0 and descent transport along the resulting equivalence of sites from D0. Those generic constructions are owned there, not recreated here.
Lift M,t,φ using the section and tensor comparisons; these carry φ(t^n)=s to the identical typed root equation in the enlarged universe. Lift h and both arrow squares in the same way.
Use the inverse carrier equivalences to recover a root and every labelled arrow, giving an actual groupoid equivalence, not a bijection of point orbits.

The supplier’s pullback comparisons transport the root pseudofunctor, κ and frame equivalence; D0’s equivalent-site transport and stackification universal property transport native-stackification-equivalence.

Underlying coherent lift maps satisfy triangle/pentagon, hence so do their root restrictions. Genuine new larger test objects are handled by the formula of the native root pseudofunctor at that universe, not asserted to come from the small site.
acceptance: The site being compared must be named, not silently enlarged.
Unit labels, including stabilizers, are transported bijectively on each matched test object.

sources.match: The root datum is intrinsic line, section and isomorphism data; universe transport is an authored formalization adapter based on the requested carrier equivalences, not a theorem printed in Appendix B.

sources.locator: Lemmas 8.9.1–8.9.3, §8.9 Tag 02ZO and Lemma 8.9.1 Tag 02ZP; online, no fixed pagination
sources.match: The stackification universal characterization transports across equivalent sites; it does not identify sites with different objects.
